description:
FILED s470bl (Opus, 2026-09-05) with the discriminating measurement already
taken.  This is the ONE thing that stops #1022 half (b) from merging.

WHAT HAPPENS.  With the dynamic-exit frame emitted, `t/op/loopctl.t` produces
NO TAP at all (companion: `P: 66/1  C: 0/0  DIFF`, empty note).  Loading its
emission by hand shows "Heap exhausted during garbage collection ... Heap
exhausted, game over" while SBCL is COMPILING, not running.  It runs and gives
67 rows at `--dynamic-space-size 1200`.

WHERE THE HEAP GOES, per top-level form (scratch/s470bl/perform.lisp reads the
file form by form and reports bytes consed):

    form #71, the file's own code, ONE `locally` of 64 KB, 88 frames
      gate OFF (-dyn-loop-exit)   244.6 MB
      gate ON                     691.2 MB
      gate ON, runtime with `(catch â¦)` replaced by `(progn â¦)`
                                  266.6 MB     <-- the discriminator

So it is the `catch` itself: ~4.8 MB of compile IR per occurrence in a form
that size.  Everything else was ruled out by measurement, not by argument:

  * NOT the nesting.  60 frames nested SIX deep cost 0.25 MB each (19.8 vs
    5.1 MB total), the same as 60 flat ones (21.2 vs 8.2).
  * NOT the frame's SHAPE.  The first version put the loop's exit targets
    OUTSIDE the catch (so each became an NLX through it); rewriting so every
    exit stays LEXICAL and the value travels out through `catch`'s own return
    value made the file cons MORE, not less (2689 vs 2589 MB in total).  The
    rewrite is kept anyway â it also removes a stack unwind per loop exit at
    run time.
  * NOT compiler policy.  `_cap_inlining_if_huge` already wraps this form in
    `(locally (declare (notinline â¦)))` â the s268 fix for the SAME class of
    blow-up â and adding `(optimize (compilation-speed 3))` or
    `(optimize (speed 0) (debug 0) (compilation-speed 3))` to that wrapper
    changes nothing (still 0 rows at 1 GB).

THE REGRESSION IS CONFINED, measured both ways:
  * the eight frame-heaviest `perl-tests` files â loopctl, sprintf2, local,
    split, magic, array, eval, aassign, 2974 rows between them â match their
    blessed baselines EXACTLY;
  * `perl-tests/loopctl.t` itself goes 40/0 -> 64/0 (fully passing), and it
    carries 88 frames too: the perl-distribution copy is the one that fails,
    because the companion run also compiles the distribution's own `t/test.pl`
    in-process first (that BEGIN form conses ~2 GB), leaving less headroom;
  * `t/op/rt119311.t` goes 8/2 -> 11/2, its pre-(a) value.

THE FIX, and it is a DESIGN CHANGE that needs a ruling.  The licence today is
the brief's: "frame a loop whose body contains a USER CALL".  In
`t/op/loopctl.t` that is 88 loops, because nearly every one calls `ok`/`is`/
`cmp_ok`.  A NARROWER licence would be: frame a loop only when it can REACH a
MARKED dynamic-exit site â the sites are known (Parser2::_mark_dynamic_loop_exits
stamps them), so the test is "the body calls a sub declared in this unit that
transitively contains a marked site, or contains an anon `sub {â¦}` that does,
or contains `eval`/`goto`/`require`/`do`/`tie`".  That takes
`t/op/loopctl.t` from 88 frames to about ONE (its `sub test_last { last }`) and
almost every ordinary file to ZERO, which also makes the whole feature free by
construction rather than by measurement.

Its COST is that a dynamic exit performed by a sub in ANOTHER compilation unit
(a module) stops working: the loop takes no frame, so the exit dies with perl's
`Can't "last" outside a loop block` instead of exiting the caller's loop.  That
failure is LOUD, and the shape is rare (a module doing a BARE `last` at sub top
level; Test::More's `skip` uses the LABELLED form, which never needed a frame).
Whether that trade is acceptable is the ruling this task needs.

The branch is `e8bfc83` in the s470bl worktree, with everything else green:
the bench A/B is 0.96-1.02x inside its own spread, the token-level emission A/B
is 0 UNEXPLAINED, emission-ab RCDIFF 0 over 1035 files, 53 probes match perl.

=== RULED BY FABLE AND IMPLEMENTED (s470bl, same session) ===
THE RULING: a loop gets a frame only if its body can REACH a marked exit site.
Per compilation unit, MAY-DYN-EXIT is the fixpoint over the call graph from the
subs that contain a marked `%p-dyn-loop-exit` site (a sub is in the set if it
contains a site or DIRECTLY calls, by name, a sub in the set); a loop is framed
iff its body contains a direct named call to a sub in that set â or lexically
contains a nested `sub {â¦}` carrying a site, which is `t/op/rt119311.t`'s
`{ foo(sub { â¦; last }) }` shape and what its 11/2 needs.  Anonymous subs
called BY COderef, method calls, `&$code`, `goto &NAME`, string eval and calls
to subs NOT declared in the unit do NOT frame the loop.

IMPLEMENTATION: `Pl::Parser2::_may_dyn_exit_set` computes the set inside
`_mark_dynamic_loop_exits` (one extra doc walk, no extra parse); it rides on
`Pl::Environment::dyn_exit_subs` because BOTH loop-lowering seams read it
(Parser2's compound loops, Pl::Parser's `for`/`while` modifiers);
`Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::may_dyn_exit` is the 14-line predicate that replaced
`calls_user_code` and its four word tables (DELETED).  Both readings are
deliberately generous â a nested sub's site counts for its enclosing sub, any
mention of a declared name counts as a call â because being wrong that way
costs one catch per loop entry, never a missing frame.

MEASURED AFTER:
  * `t/op/loopctl.t`   88 frames -> 1; 67 rows at the DEFAULT 1 GB heap;
    companion `--jobs 1` C 40/0 -> 64/3, one row BETTER than the pre-(a) 63/4.
  * `t/op/rt119311.t`  8/2 -> 11/2 (its pre-(a) value).
  * `perl-tests` corpus: 1214 frames in 93 files -> ONE frame in one file.
  * `tools/bench-exec.pl`: ALL 27 rows byte-identical with the gate on or off
    (was 21 of 27), so the bench cannot move at all.
  * token-level emission A/B vs main `34fbeab`: gate-off 49 files differ with
    the only added tokens `(block nil` (the #1160 fix), gate-on ONE file
    differs â 0 UNEXPLAINED both ways.  corpus-diff 49 of 111, silent drops 5
    unchanged, SHAPES 6 files identical.
  * ONE probe of 53 moved: `eval q{last}` inside a loop now dies into `$@`
    where perl exits the loop (the string eval is a different unit).  The
    narrowing also CLOSED #1163's one divergence.
subject: RULED + DONE (s470bl): the #1022(b) frame licence is REACHABILITY BY NAME, not "the body calls user code" â t/op/loopctl.t goes 88 frames -> 1 and produces its rows again
